oracles: reference probe (oracle-local Rust, hand-rolled filter like isofi) passes on the laptop

mutants each red: no-clone-flag-filter (unshare/clone CLONE_NEWUSER succeeds), no-denylist (socket succeeds), eperm-instead-of-kill (bpf EPERM is indistinguishable from the kernel default and must be rejected), clone3-allowed, dumpable-1, no-landlock (open outside the allowed dir succeeds), no-child-filter (fork from a forkwasm child succeeds)

acceptance.must: PASS; probe protocol documented: `<subject> --path forkwasm|cordon --probe <name>` runs the subject's own sandbox install, then the syscall, and reports one JSON line; for each probe an unfiltered control run first and host facts recorded (apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns, unprivileged_bpf_disabled, io_uring_disabled, Landlock ABI); pass only on SIGSYS (KILL_PROCESS) or ENOSYS (clone3), never EPERM; TCP_ULP probed on a pre-opened TCP fd passed by the oracle; dumpable read back via PR_GET_DUMPABLE in zygote, child and cordon

notes: Probes: clone(CLONE_NEWUSER), unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER), unshare(CLONE_NEWNET), setns, clone3, socket(AF_INET/AF_INET6/AF_UNIX/AF_NETLINK), socketpair, setsockopt(TCP_ULP,"tls"), bpf(BPF_PROG_LOAD), io_uring_setup, perf_event_open, ptrace, process_vm_readv, userfaultfd, keyctl, mount, execve, fork-from-child; landlock: open outside allowed dir, TCP connect. No `needs` (host-agnostic by construction: it judges against the recorded control), so ci/oracles.sh also runs its self-test on the desktop.
